The seeded reference store holds MSigDB human hallmark, MSigDB human GO (BP/CC/MF) and human WikiPathways as HGNC-symbol GMTs — matching the gene-symbol identifier space of counts.csv, so no ID mapping is required.
steps.question: Which hallmark and GO biological-process gene sets are coordinately shifted in drug-treated versus control human liver, given the full ranked treated-vs-control statistic?
constraints: Use the human gene set resources only — the store also holds mouse and rat versions and using them on this taxon-9606 dataset would be silently wrong
Use the ~12,000 tested genes as the background universe for any over-representation test, never the full genome
Do not pre-filter the ranked list by significance before GSEA

If a named gene set collection is absent from the environment at run time, report the collection as unavailable and continue with the ones present — do not substitute another organism or fabricate set membership
steps.description: Take the complete ranked gene statistic exported by T1S2 (shrunken log2FC, or the Wald statistic — state which, and use one consistently) over all tested genes, keyed by HGNC gene symbol, and run rank-based GSEA with fgsea. Use human gene set collections available in the environment as HGNC-symbol GMTs: the MSigDB hallmark collection (50 sets) as the primary readout, and MSigDB GO biological process as the mechanism-level follow-up. Human (not mouse or rat) gene set collections are used, and the specific collections and their set counts after size filtering are reported
Set-level BH FDR is applied within each collection, and significant sets are reported with NES, padj, set size and leading-edge genes
Redundant nested GO sets are collapsed before any count of significant processes is reported

The status of liver/xenobiotic-relevant sets (xenobiotic metabolism, bile acid metabolism, fatty acid metabolism, oxidative stress, inflammatory response) is reported explicitly, including when they are non-significant
ORA is either run with the tested-gene universe as background, or explicitly skipped with the reason stated when the DE list is too small

plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control DE (STAR/featureCounts)
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000-gene x 6-sample raw integer count matrix (counts.csv, gene symbols in the first column) from STAR + featureCounts, with metadata.csv giving one condition label per sample: 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch, human liver. Because the counts are genuine gene-level integers from featureCounts rather than transcript-level estimates from a quantifier such as salmon/kallisto, no tximport step, no length-offset and no rounding of fractional estimates are needed or appropriate — the matrix goes straight into a negative-binomial GLM. That is the one methodological fork the research question calls out, and it is settled at step T1S1.

T1S1 loads and validates the two CSVs (sample-name concordance and order, integer check, duplicate gene symbols collapsed by summing, low-count filtering), then runs QC on the design: library sizes, per-sample detected genes, VST-transformed PCA and sample-sample correlation, so a swapped label or an outlier replicate is caught before it becomes a gene list. T1S2 runs the DESeq2 Wald test for treated vs control with control as the explicit reference level. n=3 per group is the minimum for dispersion estimation: DESeq2's shrunken per-gene dispersion is the right estimator here, and the step must report the fitted dispersion trend, use lfcShrink for ranking, and state plainly that with 3v3 the analysis is powered only for large, consistent effects. T1S3 produces the reporting artefacts (volcano, MA, heatmap of top DE genes, normalized-count boxplots) and a concordance check against an independent edgeR quasi-likelihood fit — if the two methods disagree substantially on the top genes, that is a signal the effect is fragile at this sample size, and the plan says so rather than reporting one number.

T2S1 takes the full DESeq2 result as a ranked list into GSEA against human hallmark and GO-BP gene sets (staged for Homo sapiens, HGNC symbols — matching the gene-symbol identifier space of counts.csv). Rank-based GSEA rather than over-representation is deliberate: at 3v3 the FDR-significant gene list may be short or empty, and a ranked test still returns interpretable pathway-level signal from the full 12,000-gene ranking. The liver tissue and drug-treatment context makes xenobiotic-metabolism, bile-acid, fatty-acid and stress-response hallmarks the ones to inspect first, but the step must report what the data shows, not confirm that expectation.
